completion_data.completion_summary: Deployed the agent-system source store to .claude/ (16 files, making the mint-dispatch-seq persisted-counter fix and three literature hardening fixes live), removed the stale mcp__lean-lsp__* grant from the deployed install-once settings.json, and proved baseline-relatively via verify-deploy.sh that the deploy introduced zero net functional regressions.

memory_candidates.content: When diffing verify-deploy.sh (or similar) FINDING sets before/after a change with grep '^FINDING ' | sort -u plus comm -13/-23, watch for non-deterministic embedded content (e.g. a fresh mktemp -d path baked into a fix-roundtrip test's own output line) producing false deltas. Confirm by stripping the volatile token and comparing substance before concluding a comm -13 line is a genuine new regression.

A gate3 Rule S 'missing index-entries.json entry' finding that appears only after a file is deployed for the first time is not necessarily a deploy-caused regression -- it can be a pre-existing source-store gap (the file's own index-entries.json registration was never added) that was simply invisible because Rule S only evaluates already-deployed files. Check the SOURCE's own index-entries.json for the same file before classifying a newly-visible Rule S finding as a new defect.

validate-meta-write.sh's is_meta_path case list (commands/*, skills/*, agents/*, rules/*, context/*, extensions/*, scripts/*, hooks/*, */CLAUDE.md) does not cover root-level .claude/ files such as settings.json or settings.local.json. A hand-edit to a root-level install-once file will NOT trigger the source-store-boundary advisory hook, even though such an edit is exactly the kind of .claude/** write the hook exists to flag. This is a known coverage gap, not yet fixed.
